ForgeMCP persistent Landscape authorization — next alpha development

Date: October 23, 2026
Source/plugin version prepared: 0.2.17-alpha.1 (descriptor Version 31)
Disposition: IMPLEMENTED AND TESTED — PRODUCTION ACTIVATION PENDING

1. Outcome and preserved production achievement

Implemented a distinct landscape_edit_session authorization for multiple bounded native sculpts after one owner approval, with a two-hour default duration, exact process/project/ world/Landscape/layer/transform binding, explicit region/action scope, expiry and revocation. Existing one-operation adoption remains consume-once. No production grant was issued and no production Landscape write or save occurred during development.

The original production Editor remains unreal-22604 / PID 22604, running its installed 0.2.16-alpha.1 binary. It was not restarted, reloaded, hot-recompiled or replaced. Fresh final native inspection confirms the saved first riverbed is unchanged:

The file audit checked all 1,537 Content, Config and .uproject files against the saved first-riverbed baseline: zero changes, additions or missing files. Development source and the plugin version descriptor intentionally changed and are excluded from that Content/ configuration audit. Existing recovery checkpoints were not modified or restored.

2. Authorization implementation

  • Owner approval is exclusively local: Forge.Landscape.ApproveEditSession <id> opens a native identity/scope Yes/No dialog. No remote approval tool exists.
  • Default lifetime 7,200 seconds; configurable 60–86,400 seconds. Pending requests expire after 300 seconds. Grants exist only in their approving Editor/world and expire or invalidate on identity/transform/layer mismatch and world teardown.
  • Exact layer_name=ForgeTerrain and existing layer GUID are required. Layer creation, setup_layer, save, reload and arbitrary scripting are excluded from session actions.
  • A bounded region authorizes at most 1,048,576 samples. Explicit entire_landscape scope permits up to 4,194,304 and must equal the native full extent. No silent expansion.
  • Each edit and its normal halo must fit the grant. Native per-operation limits remain: heightmap 32,768 input samples, other edit chunks 1,048,576, at most eight rows per batch.
  • Immediate local/remote revocation prevents subsequent batches. Already written rows are retained with recovery evidence. Failed/cancelled jobs revoke the session rather than silently permitting further edits over an uncertain result.
  • Protected non-target layer hashes and layer order/name/visibility/lock state are checked. The target full height hash must equal the previous verified result between operations. Unexpected user edits are rejected; unsaved work is not discarded.
  • Dirty packages produced by this session may remain unsaved for subsequent operations; unrelated dirty production packages block them. One job runs at a time.

3. MCP interfaces and operation planning

Five typed tools were added and discovered in the source MCP server:

  1. unreal_landscape_edit_session_preflight
  2. unreal_request_landscape_edit_session
  3. unreal_landscape_edit_session_status
  4. unreal_revoke_landscape_edit_session
  5. unreal_read_landscape_height_region

The existing preview request now accepts edit_session_id, mutually exclusive with adoption_id. The same one-use preview/apply and native job-status protocol is preserved. Revocation is an idempotent permission-reduction operation; it is not marked read-only. Readback returns at most 32,768 native edit-layer local-cm samples in row-major order, plus region/layer/Landscape identity and raw-height checksum. It does not claim composed or collision data, and does not confer write permission.

Existing native operations remain raise, lower, flatten, smooth, generate, apply_heightmap and coastline. Hills/valleys compose bounded raise/lower falloff; riverbeds/mountain ranges use calculated heightmaps; transitions use native strength/smoothing or interpolation against bounded readback. These are explicit compositions, not new semantic terrain generators or mesh simulation. The native sequence exercised heightmap operations; it does not establish new visual/runtime acceptance for every higher-level shape.

4. Per-operation recovery and verification

Approval retains the immutable full world/external-package checkpoint. Before any edit row, each operation writes and verifies its localized before.r16 plus exact metadata, and full current in-memory snapshots of every Landscape height layer. These snapshots preserve prior unsaved session edits, which disk backups alone would miss.

Operation root: Saved/ForgeLandscape/<operation-id>. edit_session_checkpoint.json pins the layer recovery files and records exact request, identity, transform and extents; edit_session_result.json records terminal state, rows and full target hash. Status returns these recovery roots/results. Recovery file mismatch/missing data blocks writes; failures retain evidence without automatic restoration or cleanup.

Each stage retains existing stale-before/readback checks, plus editing-session permission and recovery checks. Completion verifies the full target height array against the predicted full result and all protected layer hashes. Failures stop the session. Full recovery read/write verification adds CPU/disk cost and up to 16 MiB of temporary array buffers beyond the existing plan/stage budget, plus native texture/derived-data allocations. No production latency/performance acceptance or full restore/reopen result is claimed.

5. Save boundary and compatibility limitation

This alpha supports multiple UNSAVED edits per approval. It does not authorize saving. A save or external disk edit invalidates the immutable approval checkpoint for subsequent operations; the session does not silently rebase. A new clean checkpoint and owner approval are then required. This is a deliberate boundary of the current implementation, not a claim of seamless editing across save/reload boundaries. Each session/global job history is bounded at 64 operations; history is not automatically discarded.

Use a separately reviewed scoped save workflow after ending/revoking an editing session. The existing rollback-capable save adapter was not changed or invoked. It must not be used when automatic production restoration is prohibited. Collision and independent disk-reload acceptance remain separate from height-array and authorization testing.

The legacy isolated-acceptance launcher remains pinned to its historical 0.2.16 manifest contract. It was not silently broadened. Python server package versioning is separate from the native plugin descriptor version. No new third-party dependency was added.

Native tests:

  • Forge.Landscape.Adoption.Authorization — legacy single-use and identity policy.
  • Forge.Landscape.Adoption.BackupIntegrity — legacy checkpoint corruption/missing checks.
  • Forge.Landscape.EditSession.Authorization — repeated operation eligibility, expiry, revocation and action/region/identity policy.
  • Forge.Landscape.EditSession.RecoveryIntegrity — exclusive recovery manifest, verified fixture files, tampering rejection and retained failure evidence.
  • Forge.Landscape.EditSession.IsolatedNativeSequence — actual two-layer 8 × 8 native non-World-Partition Landscape in a guarded disposable host. It exercises real request/preflight with a 7,200-second explicit whole-fixture scope, verifies pending requests cannot approve themselves, then models an owner-accepted fixture grant. It applies two real heightmaps without another approval/save, verifies Original preservation and the first unsaved edit in the second operation's recovery snapshot, reads actual quantized height through the new API, rejects wrong project/Landscape/layer/region/expiry, and revokes a third job before its first batch. The third writes zero rows and retains recovery evidence.

The final fixture's two completed operations are 1A30AE6743BAB2C67DDA298256F40E97 and A785BE3C4606993E999F75A34C65AF91. Their common fixture editing session is 40815FE04016A42CB0AD288FFF5EB3F8. The revoked third operation is E53739DD418B04319E871DB022FE56C7. These are disposable test identities, not production approvals. Automated tests do not click or prove the human approval dialog. All test processes exited; only the original production Editor remains running.

Earlier evidence is retained: the first full suite caught the missing new revocation annotation expectation; it was corrected. A native compile caught unbraced UE_LOG macro use; it was corrected. The original backup fixture failed under redirected UserDir because its source lay outside ProjectDir; its fixture path was corrected to project-local Saved, preserving the production guard. Final builds/tests above supersede those intermediate failures. A minimal-host EnhancedInput dependency warning was observed; compilation/link succeeded and production project plugin settings were not changed.

7. Source changes

implementation_manifest.json records hashes of the 15 task files:

  • Plugins/Forge/MajesticForge.uplugin — staged alpha version.
  • Plugins/Forge/Source/MajesticForge/Private/ForgeLandscape.h/.cpp — session integration, full result validation, per-job logging and bounded native height readback.
  • ForgeLandscapeAdoption.inl — shared identity/checkpoint primitives, distinct session mode, local approval/revocation and one-use compatibility.
  • ForgeLandscapeEditSession.inl — session validation, operation checkpoints and controls.
  • ForgeLandscapeAdoptionTests.inl — portable project-local legacy backup fixture.
  • ForgeLandscapeEditSessionTests.inl — new policy/recovery/native sequence tests.
  • MajesticForgeModule.cpp — native command dispatch/capability discovery.
  • server/core/landscape.py and landscape_edit_session.py — typed operation/session/read schemas.
  • server/core/connections.py and server/main.py — allowlist and MCP entry points.
  • tests/test_landscape_edit_session.py and test_mcp_stdio.py — schema/control/discovery coverage.
  • docs/landscape_edit_sessions.md — exact workflow, limits, compatibility and recovery.

The working tree already contained earlier adoption/connection work. It was preserved; the aggregate git diff is not attributed entirely to this task. Task source backups are under the evidence root before/. No commit, publication or distribution-license change was performed.

8. New workflow and remaining activation gate

After controlled activation, rediscover the Editor and five tools. Inspect exact identity, layer GUID/extent, clean production packages and current terrain data. Submit preflight and request with an explicit action list, layer and region; the owner runs the returned ApproveEditSession command and confirms the local dialog once. Verify live approved state and checkpoint. For each instruction, read/compute, preview, check bounds, apply once, poll, verify full results and retain recovery. Query status or revoke at any time. No additional approval is required between valid unsaved operations within that session.

The new compiled DLL is staged under the evidence HostProject/Plugins/Forge/Binaries/Win64; it was not copied over the running production plugin. Source MCP discovery was verified in a fresh real stdio subprocess; this chat's already-running MCP host and production native endpoint have not been refreshed to expose/activate the new interfaces. A later owner-controlled native installation/Editor activation and MCP refresh must verify that specific client/endpoint. Do not hot-swap a loaded DLL or infer live activation from source tests. No production editing-session request was issued during development.

IMPLEMENTED AND TESTED — PRODUCTION ACTIVATION PENDING. Native multi-operation editing and recovery are demonstrated in isolation. The saved production riverbed remains intact. Production/World Partition multi-operation acceptance, approval-dialog acceptance, collision, independent saved/reloaded persistence, and Phase 6C release acceptance are not claimed by this development stage.
